newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Bank of Ireland to move NY operations to Dublin.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Ireland to move NY operations to Dublin.

text.p: Bank of Ireland said on Friday that it will close its wholesale branch operation in New York and consolidate its U.S.-based corporate banking and treasury businesses in Dublin.

Bank of Ireland Asset Management, based in Greenwich, Connecticut and a leading provider of international equity management expertise in the U.S., is not affected by the announcement, Bank of Ireland said in a statement.

The bank said the decision resulted from a strategic review carried out by the group over recent months which concluded that a comparable service could be provided to its corporate and treasury clients from its base in Dublin's International Financial Services Centre (IFSC).
"Technological advances in recent years have greatly reduced the significance of geographical location for such operations," Brian Goggin, chief executive of corporate and treasury, said.
"The IFSC infrastructure and the skilled team we have assembled there allow us to provide a very high standard of service to clients, wherever they may be located."
